---
title: "Getting support"
last-reviewed: "2026-09-06"
---

If workload, health or someone's behaviour is making research difficult, you can ask for support before you have worked out every detail. Start with the service that fits the problem.

## Urgent help {#first-response}

For immediate danger, contact local emergency services. For an urgent health concern, contact an appropriate health service.

## Find a contact {#choose-the-authorised-route}

| What is happening | A place to start |
|---|---|
| Distress, illness, disability or an unmanageable workload | Student wellbeing, a health practitioner or your university's accessibility service. Your graduate research office can explain leave and candidature adjustments. |
| Bullying, harassment, discrimination or a legal concern | A confidential student adviser, independent complaints service or qualified legal adviser. |
| Participant harm, unsafe laboratory or field work, or pressure to work outside approval | The relevant safety or ethics contact. |
| A privacy breach, lost data or compromised account | Your institution's privacy, IT security or research data service. |
| Suspected research misconduct | Your research integrity adviser or the institution's designated confidential contact. |

Contact names vary between universities. If you're unsure, ask a confidential student support service to help you find the right one.

## Prepare what you can {#preserve-only-what-is-safe}

Keep factual dates, events and relevant messages in an approved confidential location, if it is safe to do so. You don't need to investigate the matter yourself or confront anyone before seeking advice. Leave identifying details and allegations out of public GitHub suggestions and shared project tools.

[]{#ask-for-a-concrete-protection-or-decision}

Tell the adviser what help you need now: confidential advice, a workload adjustment, leave, a different supervision contact, protection of access or an incident assessment. The [message template](../templates/escalation-message.qmd) can help you put this into words when it is safe to use.

## Follow up {#evidence-of-next-state}

Ask who will respond and when. If an urgent concern hasn't been acknowledged, contact the service again or use its urgent route. Keep track of agreed protections and the next contact.
